title: Enterprise usage & cost dashboard intake: triage plan and prioritization rubric
creator: Lena Marshall
description: Consolidate incoming enterprise requests for usage analytics, per-team cost breakdowns, and exportable dashboard artifacts into a repeatable triage flow. Define a prioritization rubric that balances regulatory needs, startup PLG signals, and Dedicated/Private customer contracts. Outcome: a short-lived intake catalog, a scoring rubric, and proposed scope for a minimum viable dashboard + CSV/BigQuery exports.
acceptance_criteria: A documented intake template for usage/cost/reporting requests linked from support and customer success
A 4-factor prioritization rubric (Compliance, Financial Impact, Frequency, Implementation Effort) with scoring thresholds
A triage decision log with at least 8 recent enterprise requests scored and dispositioned
A clear recommended MVP scope for console: 1) per-API-key daily usage timeline, 2) top-10 cost contributors by model/route, 3) CSV/BigQuery export, and 4) role-based access knob
Stakeholder sign-off from CS, Sales AE lead, and Infra PM
proposed_priority_rationale: Requests span critical enterprise contract clauses (billing exports for audits) and repeated sales blockers. High financial visibility can reduce churn and unlock Dedicated commitments; therefore prioritize above low-frequency vanity metrics. Implementation leverages existing cost telemetry tables, keeping infra lift moderate (est 2-3 sprints).
stakeholder_requests: Large fintech customer: nightly CSV of per-tenant token usage for audit and invoicing
Platform team: per-model cost trend breakdown to recommend quantization and routing policies
Enterprise AE: on-demand export for customer finance team (csv + BigQuery push)
Compliance team: immutable access log and export for data residency audits
analysis_summary: Reviewed 14 incoming requests from CS, support tickets SUP-3321 and SUP-3399, and two AE escalation threads. Common patterns: need for scheduled exports, per-tenant cost attribution, and role-filtered dashboards. Technical feasibility is strong: serving runtime emits per-request token metrics; flow gaps are mostly in aggregation, UI filters, and export plumbing. Risk: multi-tenant cost attribution for routed fallbacks requires alignment with routing policy metadata.
